verdict.rationale: Mercury Books' own docs show that its Command assistant can do work like "organizing your chart of accounts", so the product itself offers some chart-of-accounts management, though the depth is unproven. The only evidence of Classes concerns attaching them to Mercury transactions for customers syncing to QuickBooks or NetSuite. That is an external-ledger integration, not a dimension inside Books, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: documented creation and customization of accounts with account types, sub-account hierarchy, class/tag dimensions within Books itself, and any hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an accountant, I can customize the chart of accounts with account types, sub-accounts, and class or tag dimensions

citations.quote: Offload work like writing journal entries, organizing your chart of accounts, categorization in bulk, and more.
